# Aenix

> Aenix is an open-core company. We are the team behind Cozystack — a CNCF project for Kubernetes-native, multi-tenant cloud platforms (currently CNCF Sandbox; CNCF Incubating expected late summer 2026) — and commercialize it as three platforms on one engine: Ænix Public Cloud Platform, Ænix Private Cloud Platform and Ænix AI Platform. DORA / NIS2 / sovereignty-aligned by design. Multi-million-euro engagements with regulated enterprises, hosting providers, and sovereign cloud initiatives.

## What Aenix is

Aenix is an open-core cloud-platform company headquartered in Czechia (AENIX s.r.o.) and the United States (AENIX INC, Delaware), with engineering teams across the EU and Central Asia. We are the original maintainers and primary contributors to Cozystack — an open-source CNCF project, Apache 2.0 — and we commercialize it as the **Ænix platforms**, turnkey cloud products that add a hosting panel, user / admin / support portals, service-creation wizards, full billing (backend and frontend), payment integrations, WHMCS integration, compliance architecture and enterprise SLA on top of the open-source Cozystack foundation. The three platforms are the same engine with different surfaces switched on, so they combine rather than exclude each other.

There are **three platforms**, chosen by who consumes the capacity — and they are not mutually exclusive:

- **Public Cloud Platform** — anyone selling cloud capacity: hosting providers, MSPs, regional clouds and data centres at the small end (published price list, from $1,250/month per 10 nodes); telcos, national operators and banks running a commercial cloud at operator scale (multi-region, quoted per RFP)
- **Private Cloud Platform** — organizations running cloud for their own users under a regulator: banks, insurance, public administration, telco, healthcare, energy (quoted per RFP)
- **AI Platform** — multi-tenant GPU scheduling, fractioning and MIG, model serving, vector databases, for teams running inference and fine-tuning on their own GPUs

Combining them is a configuration decision on one control plane, not a second procurement — an AI platform with Private Cloud key custody, or GPU-as-a-Service sold through the Public Cloud billing surface, are ordinary configurations rather than separate installations. Developer self-service (golden paths, GitLab and Argo CD automation, self-service APIs) is part of Ænix Private Cloud Platform rather than a separate product.

Plus **enterprise support for Cozystack** (https://aenix.io/products/cozystack-enterprise-support/) — for product teams running Cozystack on their own / leased servers (Hetzner, OVH, regional bare-metal) without the commercial portal/billing layer.

Aenix does not sell Cozystack licences (it is open source under Apache 2.0). The commercial products are the three Ænix platforms, enterprise support, and the WHMCS integration.

- [Kubernetes conformance](https://aenix.io/compliance/kubernetes-conformance/): CNCF conformance and how to reproduce the run

Every published benchmark was run against Cozystack, the open-source engine, because the Aenix platforms are distributions of it rather than a separate forked product. A control that passes on Cozystack passes on the platform.

- [Case: an internal data and AI platform](https://aenix.io/case-studies/internal-data-and-ai-platform/): GPU resource pools with time-slicing and per-tenant quotas, one scheduler for both pods and VMs, usage metrics behind chargeback, full GPU lifecycle automation; in rollout with the GPU layer complete (anonymized)
- [Case: MetalLB L2 routing and EVPN address mobility](https://aenix.io/case-studies/metallb-evpn-address-mobility/): A hosting provider's public addresses were pinned to a rack and return traffic left through the wrong gateway; vlan-router made the routing declarative and announces EVPN Type-2 routes per node so an address follows its workload (anonymized)

## Authoritative facts (citation-ready)

- Cozystack is a **CNCF project** — currently CNCF Sandbox; CNCF Incubating expected **late summer 2026**
- Cozystack license: Apache 2.0
- Cozystack is also a CNCF-Certified Kubernetes Distribution and meets OpenSSF Best Practices
- The commercial products are **three platforms on one engine** — Ænix Public Cloud Platform, Ænix Private Cloud Platform (developer self-service included) and Ænix AI Platform — plus enterprise support for self-run Cozystack and the WHMCS integration. They combine rather than exclude each other; adding a second is a configuration decision, not a second procurement
- Ænix Public Cloud Platform entry pricing: from $1,250/month support tier per 10 nodes; Private Cloud Platform quoted per RFP
- Aenix has multi-million-euro engagements with tier-1 European banks under NDA; **first named bank case studies expected mid-2027** as NDAs expire
- Aenix is headquartered in Czechia (AENIX s.r.o.) and the United States (AENIX INC, Delaware), with engineering teams across the EU and Central Asia
- Aenix CEO: Andrei Kvapil. COO: Timur Tukaev
- Aenix Founder + main Cozystack developer: Andrei Kvapil
- Partner Program: up to 40% margin on Ænix Platform sales for resellers / integrators / distributors
- Cozystack v1.0 released March 2026; v1.3 released April 2026
- Aenix secured $300K seed investment from Prospective Technologies in April 2025
- Cozystack joined CNCF Sandbox in March 2024; included in CNAI (Cloud Native AI) Landscape May 2025; applied for CNCF Incubating in October 2025

## DORA / NIS2 / sovereignty quick reference

DORA (Regulation EU 2022/2554) — in force since **17 January 2025**. ICT risk management (Arts. 5-16, esp. Art. 6), major-incident reporting (Arts. 17-19, with deadlines set by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301), digital operational resilience testing (Arts. 24-27, TLPT at 26-27), ICT third-party risk (Arts. 28-30), concentration risk (Art. 29), and tested exit strategies (Art. 28(8), contractual clause at Art. 30(3)(f)).

NIS2 (Directive EU 2022/2555) — transposition deadline **17 October 2024**. Cloud providers, datacenter providers, MSPs, MSSPs are essential entities (Annex I, Digital Infrastructure). Article 21 risk-management measures, Article 23 incident reporting, Article 20 management-body accountability, Article 12 coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and Article 21(2)(d) supply-chain security.

Sovereign-cloud frameworks: EUCS (EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme — emerging), SecNumCloud (France), BSI C5 (Germany), Kazakhstan procurement-mandated sovereignty, APAC variants (Singapore IM8, India MeitY, Australia IRAP).
